clean: Dear Mr. Linkfist, thank you for your email, and I'm sorry to hear about the problems with your e-bike since the service. I've spoken to the mechanic who worked on it, Culmeck, and looked at the job sheet. We replaced the brake rotors and bled the rear brake, but it looks like the motor error you're describing, error code 31, isn't related to anything we touched. Having said that, I completely understand why it feels like it started after the visit. What I'd suggest is that you bring it back in this week and we'll run the manufacturer's diagnostic at no charge. If the fault turns out to be from the service, we'll fix it for free, and if it's the motor, we'll handle the warranty claim with the manufacturer for you so you don't have to. We're open Tuesday to Saturday, 9 till 6, and on Saturdays we close at 5:30. Kind regards, Benedict Burg, Workshop Manager

Can you help me think through whether solar makes sense for our house? Here are the details. We're in central Ohio, the roof faces southeast, it's about 12 years old and asphalt shingle, and we use roughly 11,000 kilowatt hours a year, mostly because we have an electric heat pump and one electric car. We've had two quotes. One is for an 8.4 kilowatt system at $23,000 before the tax credit, the other is 9.6 kilowatts for $26,500, also before the credit. Neither includes a battery. My worries are whether we should replace the roof first, how long the pay is, and whether net metering in our area is going to get worse. Please walk me through the numbers step by step and tell me what other information you'd need to give a real answer.

Write a short synopsis for our festival catalog, about 60 words, for a documentary we're screening. Years well I know about it. It's called The Salt Road, it runs 92 minutes, and it's directed by Margery Quayle, it's her first feature. It follows two generations of a family of salt harvesters on the coast of Britain over one summer, as the youngest daughter decides whether to stay and take over the salt pans or move to Paris for university. There's no narration, it's all observational, and the cinematography is stunning, lots of long white shots of the marshes at dawn. I don't want the synopsis to give away what she decides. Also, avoid words like point and ten breathtaking, every single synopsis in the catalog uses them. And give me two versions, one more lyrical and one more straightforward.

I'd like some honest advice, not a pep talk. I'm 38, I've worked in insurance claims for about 15 years, and I'm good at it, but I'm completely bored. For the past two years I've been working weekends at a friend's bike shop, mostly doing wheel builds and basic repairs, and it's the only part of my week I actually look forward to. The owner I'm retiring in two years and had hinted that he'd sell me the business, but I've never run anything and I have a mortgage and two kids. I'm not asking you to tell me what to do. What I want is a list of the questions I should be able to answer before I even have a serious conversation with you, about the finances, about my family, and about whether I'd still love fixing bikes if it was my whole job. And if there are common mistakes people make buying a small business from a friend, tell me those too.
